key_facts: Normal growth and development for age and sex
Initial exam showed multiple areas of erythema, vesicles, and bullae
Vital signs were within normal ranges
Skin-punch biopsy revealed hyperkeratosis and bullae formation within the epidermis
Genetic testing revealed a heterozygous variation c.482T>C (p. L161P) in KRT1
Later developed thickened, brown, corrugated plaques and palmoplantar hyperkeratosis

raw.rationale: The patient's skin lesions, hyperkeratosis, and bullae formation within the epidermis, along with the genetic testing revealing a heterozygous variation in KRT1, are consistent with Epidermolytic Hyperkeratosis.

rejected.label: Bullous Congenital Ichthyosiform Erythroderma
rejected.why: While similar, the specific genetic variation and clinical presentation are more closely aligned with Epidermolytic Hyperkeratosis.

rejected.label: Ichthyosis Bullosa of Siemens
rejected.why: The clinical features and genetic findings do not perfectly match Ichthyosis Bullosa of Siemens, which typically involves different mutations and presentations.

rejected.label: Superficial Epidermolytic Ichthyosis
rejected.why: The depth of skin involvement and specific genetic mutation point more towards Epidermolytic Hyperkeratosis than Superficial Epidermolytic Ichthyosis.
